en: This app is easy to use even for beginners.
tamil: இந்த ஆப்பை ஆரம்பிக்கிறவங்களும் ஈஸியா யூஸ் பண்ணலாம்.
context: Recommending an app to a friend.
explain: 'Easy to use' describes a simple tool. 'Even for' adds a surprise.
usage: Say it when you suggest an app to someone new to technology.
leelaQ: Which app would you suggest to a beginner?
answer: I would suggest a simple app like WhatsApp.

en: The phone was on silent, so I missed your call.
tamil: போன் சைலண்ட்ல இருந்துச்சு, அதனால உன் கால் மிஸ் ஆயிடுச்சு.
explain: 'Missed' is the past of 'miss'. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Say it to friends or family when they are upset about a call.
leelaQ: Do you keep your phone on silent?
answer: Only in meetings, otherwise I keep it on loud.

en: I forgot to attach the file to the email.
tamil: நான் மெயில்ல ஃபைலை அட்டாச் பண்ண மறந்துட்டேன்.
explain: 'Forgot to' plus a verb means you did not do something you should have done.
usage: Say it at work before sending a second email.
leelaQ: What mistakes do you make in emails?
answer: I sometimes forget the attachment or the subject.

en: My neighbour is fixing my TV remote.
tamil: என் பக்கத்து வீட்டுக்காரர் என் டிவி ரிமோட்டை சரிசெய்றாங்க.
context: Telling a visitor what is happening.
explain: Present continuous is used for something happening now.
usage: Use it in casual talk about gadgets at home.
leelaQ: Can you fix small things at home?
answer: Yes, I can fix a switch or change a bulb.

en: I am not comfortable sharing my phone number online.
tamil: என் போன் நம்பரை ஆன்லைன்ல பகிர எனக்கு வசதியா இல்ல.
explain: 'Comfortable doing' shows how you feel. 'Not' makes it negative.
usage: Say it when a website or a stranger asks for personal details.
leelaQ: What information should we not share online?
answer: We should not share passwords or our home address.

en: Do not forget to charge your laptop before the meeting.
tamil: மீட்டிங்குக்கு முன்னாடி உன் லேப்டாப்பை சார்ஜ் பண்ண மறந்துடாதே.
explain: 'Do not forget to' plus a verb is a friendly reminder.
usage: Use it before a long meeting or a trip.
leelaQ: What do you do before an important meeting?
answer: I charge my laptop and test my camera.

en: I don't use social media during exam time.
tamil: நான் தேர்வு நேரத்துல சோஷியல் மீடியா யூஸ் பண்றதில்ல.
context: Explaining a good habit to a friend.
explain: 'Don't' makes present simple negative with I, you, we and they.
usage: Say it when talking about focus and study habits.
leelaQ: Does social media waste your time?
answer: Sometimes it does, so I limit it to thirty minutes a day.

en: Hello, can everyone see my screen?
tamil: ஹலோ, எல்லாருக்கும் என் ஸ்கிரீன் தெரியுதா?
explain: 'Can everyone...?' checks with a group. It is a common meeting phrase.
usage: Say it just after you start sharing your screen.
leelaQ: What do you say at the start of a presentation?
answer: I say hello and ask if everyone can hear me.

en: Which phone is better for a small budget?
tamil: சின்ன பட்ஜெட்டுக்கு எந்த போன் நல்லது?
explain: 'Which' is used when choosing from a few options.
usage: Ask at a mobile shop or from a friend who knows phones.
leelaQ: What is a good budget for a phone?
answer: About fifteen thousand rupees is a good budget for me.

en: How much data do I have left?
tamil: எனக்கு எவ்வளவு டேட்டா மீதி இருக்கு?
explain: 'How much' is used for things we cannot count, like data.
usage: Ask at a mobile store or in an app at the end of the month.
leelaQ: How much data do you use every day?
answer: I use about two GB every day.

en: When did the update finish?
tamil: அப்டேட் எப்போ முடிஞ்சுது?
explain: 'When did' asks about the time of a past event. After 'did', use the base verb.
usage: Use it in the office when a system was down for maintenance.
leelaQ: What do you do while an update is running?
answer: I drink tea and wait.

en: Why is my phone getting so hot?
tamil: என் போன் ஏன் இவ்வளவு சூடாகுது?
explain: 'Why' asks for a reason. 'Getting hot' shows a change.
usage: Ask a technician or a friend when your phone overheats.
leelaQ: What makes a phone hot?
answer: Playing games for a long time makes it hot.

en: Are you free for a quick video call?
tamil: உனக்கு ஒரு சின்ன வீடியோ கால் பண்ண நேரம் இருக்கா?
context: Asking a colleague for a short call.
explain: 'Are you free?' asks if someone has time.
usage: Use it with coworkers before you call them.
leelaQ: When do you prefer to have calls?
answer: I prefer calls in the evening after work.

en: Who is hosting the meeting today?
tamil: இன்னைக்கு மீட்டிங்கை யார் ஹோஸ்ட் பண்றாங்க?
explain: 'Hosting' means running the meeting.
usage: Ask it when you cannot find the link.
leelaQ: Who usually leads your meetings?
answer: My manager usually leads them.

en: Did you see the message in the group?
tamil: க்ரூப்ல வந்த மெசேஜை பாத்தியா?
context: Asking a friend about a group chat.
explain: 'Did you see...?' asks about a past action.
usage: Ask classmates or coworkers about news in a group chat.
leelaQ: Are you in many WhatsApp groups?
answer: Yes, I am in about ten groups.

en: What is the Wi-Fi name and password?
tamil: வைஃபை பேரு என்ன, பாஸ்வேர்டு என்ன?
context: Asking at a cafe or a friend's house.
explain: Wi-Fi names are called SSIDs, but people simply say 'Wi-Fi name'.
usage: A very common question when you visit a place and need the internet.
leelaQ: Where do you ask for the Wi-Fi password?
answer: I ask the staff at a cafe or my friend at home.

en: Will the app work without internet?
tamil: இன்டர்நெட் இல்லாம இந்த ஆப் வேலை செய்யுமா?
explain: 'Will' asks about the future. 'Without' means not having.
usage: Ask before you travel to a place with weak signal.
leelaQ: Which apps do you use offline?
answer: I use music and notes apps offline.

en: Is it safe to pay through this link?
tamil: இந்த லிங்க் வழியா பணம் கட்டுறது பாதுகாப்பானதா?
explain: 'Is it safe to...?' asks about safety.
usage: Ask a family member or a bank when you are not sure about a payment.
leelaQ: How do you pay for things online?
answer: I pay with UPI because it is quick and simple.

en: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
tamil: நீ அதை ஆஃப் பண்ணிட்டு திரும்ப ஆன் பண்ணிப் பாத்தியா?
explain: 'Have you tried...?' asks about experience. It uses the -ing form after 'tried'.
usage: Help desk staff say this first for almost every problem.
leelaQ: What is your first step when a device does not work?
answer: I restart it and check the cables.

en: Could you speak a little louder? The sound is low.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் சத்தமா பேச முடியுமா? சவுண்ட் கம்மியா இருக்கு.
context: Asking a speaker in an online meeting.
explain: 'A little louder' makes the request soft. The second sentence gives the reason.
usage: Use it when you cannot hear someone on a call.
leelaQ: Do you speak clearly on calls?
answer: I try to speak slowly and clearly.

en: Please help me to download this app.
tamil: இந்த ஆப்பை டவுன்லோட் பண்ண எனக்கு உதவி பண்ணுங்க.
context: Asking a younger person for help.
explain: 'Help me to' plus a verb is polite when you say 'please'.
usage: Say it to a child or a friend who is good with technology.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for help with apps?
answer: I ask my nephew because he knows many apps.

en: Could you put the link in the chat box?
tamil: லிங்கை சாட் பாக்ஸ்ல போட முடியுமா?
explain: 'Could you put...' is polite. 'Chat box' is the area for messages in a call.
usage: Use it in a video call when a speaker mentions a link.
leelaQ: What do people usually write in the chat box?
answer: They write questions and links.

en: Please switch on your camera for a minute.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு ஒரு நிமிஷம் உங்க கேமராவை ஆன் பண்ணுங்க.
explain: 'Switch on' is the same as 'turn on'.
usage: A teacher or an interviewer says this during an online session.
leelaQ: Do you like to keep your camera on?
answer: Not always, but I keep it on in interviews.

en: Can you teach me how to use Excel?
tamil: எக்ஸெல்லை எப்படி யூஸ் பண்றதுன்னு எனக்கு சொல்லித் தர முடியுமா?
explain: 'How to' plus a verb asks for a method.
usage: Ask a colleague when you must learn a new office tool.
leelaQ: What computer skill do you want to learn?
answer: I want to learn Excel for my work.

en: Please speak slowly, the network is breaking.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு மெதுவா பேசுங்க, நெட்வொர்க் கட் ஆகுது.
explain: 'Breaking' means the signal is cutting in and out.
usage: Say it on a phone call when the signal is weak.
leelaQ: Where is your phone signal weak?
answer: The signal is weak in our basement.
